sites.evidence_type: published tolerance of a different insertion (transposon, FP fusion)
sites.functional_impact_measured: Patch-clamp electrophysiology in HEK-293 cells: GABA-A receptor function preserved (physiological currents recorded); surface display confirmed by continuous membrane fluorescence in non-permeabilized cells.
sites.rationale: The paper names residue S181 (their numbering) as the best-performing ncAA incorporation site, with patch-clamp confirming preserved receptor function (L3) and surface fluorescence confirming membrane display (L2). The paper's numbering does not match canonical UniProt positions: canonical 181=P and canonical 201=N are not serines. A systematic search of all serine residues in the extracellular domain (29-251) shows that the unique offset of +32 maps paper S181 -> canonical 213 (S) and paper S201 -> canonical 233 (S), the only pair of serine residues in the EC domain separated by exactly 20 residues. Canonical 213 is 39 residues from TM1 (252) and 185 residues from the signal-peptide cleavage site. insert_after_residue=212 places the tag at the validated serine position. Full-length GABA-A receptor alpha-2 subunit expressed in HEK-293 cells; amber stop codon (TAG) introduced at S181 (paper numbering; canonical S213 after correcting for the paper's 32-aa signal-peptide offset) in the large N-terminal extracellular domain; ncAA incorporated via genetic code expansion and labeled with tetrazine-dye conjugates (Me-tet-Cy5 / Me-tet-CF568). Continuous fluorescence signal along the cell membrane confirmed surface display.

sources.claim: Next, we performed patch-clamp experiments in HEK-293 cells expressing the mutant α2 S181TAG, which showed the highest labeling efficiency on the equatorial cell membrane ( Figure 2 ), to demonstrate that the chosen ncAA incorporation site preserves physiological GABA-A receptor function ( Figure 3 ).

sites.evidence_type: published tolerance of a different insertion (transposon, FP fusion)
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by continuous membrane fluorescence in non-permeabilized cells (L2). No electrophysiology reported specifically for the S201TAG construct.
sites.rationale: The paper names S201 (their numbering) as one of the two best-performing ncAA incorporation sites, with surface display confirmed by membrane fluorescence (L2). Applying the same +32 offset as for S181 (see site 1 rationale), paper S201 maps to canonical 233 (S), which is 19 residues from TM1 (252) and 205 residues from the signal-peptide cleavage site, well within the extracellular domain (29-251). insert_after_residue=232 places the tag at the validated serine position; no function assay was reported for this specific mutant. Full-length GABA-A receptor alpha-2 subunit expressed in HEK-293 cells; amber stop codon (TAG) introduced at S201 (paper numbering; canonical S233 after correcting for the paper's 32-aa signal-peptide offset) in the large N-terminal extracellular domain; ncAA incorporated via genetic code expansion and labeled with tetrazine-dye conjugates. Continuous fluorescence signal along the cell membrane confirmed surface display.

sources.claim: Here, Amber mutants S181TAG and S201TAG showed the most efficient labeling demonstrated by a continuous fluorescence signal visible along the cell membrane ( Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure 2 ).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-HA antibody labeling of non-permeabilized cells (Alexa Fluor 488/555/647 and CF568 conjugates); also used in dual-color dSTORM. No electrophysiology reported for the HA-tagged construct specifically.
sites.rationale: The paper describes an HA tag at the 'n-terminal part' of the full-length alpha-2 subunit, confirmed on the cell surface by antibody labeling of intact non-permeabilized cells (L4, L5, L6). No residue number is stated, but the mature N-terminus (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 28) is the only extracellular N-terminal position available; insert_after_residue=28 is the topology-derived junction (residue_before=A, residue_after=N). The large extracellular domain (29-251, 223 residues from TM1) provides ample space for an HA or ALFA tag at this terminus. Full-length GABA-A receptor alpha-2 subunit expressed in HEK-293 cells; HA tag placed at the 'n-terminal part of the protein' (paper's words) and used as a positive control for genetic code expansion. Anti-HA antibody labeling of non-permeabilized cells confirmed surface display of the tagged full-length protein.

sources.claim: Antibody labeling of HA-tag (green) serves as positive control for GCE as the HA tag is located at the n-terminal part of the protein and expression of HA-tag is only feasible after successful ncAA incorporation.

literature_notes: Three sites are supported by the ledger (PMC8664562). The paper's residue numbering for S181 and S201 does not match canonical UniProt positions (canonical 181=P, 201=N). A systematic search of all serine residues in the extracellular domain (29-251) shows that the unique consistent offset is +32: paper S181 -> canonical 213 (S) and paper S201 -> canonical 233 (S), the only pair of serines in the EC domain separated by exactly 20 residues. This offset likely reflects the paper's use of a signal-peptide prediction of 32 aa (vs. the 28 aa computed by the topology landmarks). The ncAA incorporation (genetic code expansion) is a point modification, not a peptide-tag insertion, but it directly validates surface accessibility and functional tolerance at these positions, qualifying as 'published tolerance of a different insertion'. The HA tag at the N-terminus is topology-derived (no residue named in the paper) but the mature N-terminus (after SP cleavage at residue 28) is the only extracellular N-terminal position. Ledger lines L1, L5, and L6 provide supporting context but do not add new sites beyond those grounded in L2, L3, and L4.
